answer: A concrete defense is karst-shaped admission: each credential lands in a sinkhole whose capacity derives from hashing its genesis seed, so placement is unchoosable. A sinkhole admits one active credential per epoch, and a newcomer entering an occupied hole must present an ember release token, which the incumbent burns and the ledger records as a signal event tying both identities. A farm cannot precompute hole depths, and each clone squeezed in consumes capacity and leaves a linked trail. Density has a hard ceiling, and linkage makes clusters visible to auditors afterwards.
